title: Integration Patterns, Cost Optimization, KPIs/ROI, and Cloud-First Design
bodyMarkdown:
## Integration patterns and data movement

Decoupling a monolith or connecting systems comes down to a handful of patterns. The Well-Architected [system design principles](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/system-design) say why: decoupled components are upgraded, secured and tuned independently.

| Pattern | Service | Use for |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Asynchronous messaging and event fan-out | **Pub/Sub** | One event, many consumers; decouple producers from consumers |
| Managed batch and streaming pipelines | **Dataflow** | Code-based ETL at scale with Apache Beam |
| Visual, code-free data integration | **Cloud Data Fusion** | Build pipelines in a web UI without writing code |
| Service orchestration | **Workflows** | Serverless sequencing of HTTP calls and Google Cloud APIs |
| Scheduled, dependency-rich pipelines | **Cloud Composer (now Managed Service for Apache Airflow)** | Python DAGs across clouds and on-premises |
| API exposure | **API Gateway**, **Apigee** | Simple REST façade versus governed API program |
| Change data capture | **Datastream**, **Database Migration Service** | Replicate or migrate operational data |

[Pub/Sub](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview) is an asynchronous, scalable messaging service that decouples the services producing messages from those processing them, with typical latencies on the order of 100 milliseconds. Each subscription receives messages independently, so adding a consumer needs no producer change; subscription types include pull, push, BigQuery, Bigtable and Cloud Storage. Delivery is at-least-once (exactly-once is optional), so consumers should be idempotent.

[Dataflow](https://cloud.google.com/dataflow/docs/overview) provides unified stream and batch processing as a fully managed service built on Apache Beam (Java, Python, Go), with autoscaling, prebuilt templates and exactly-once processing by default. [Cloud Data Fusion](https://cloud.google.com/data-fusion/docs/concepts/overview) is the visual alternative: a managed service on open source CDAP that runs pipelines on ephemeral Spark clusters. Dataflow suits code and streaming; Data Fusion suits drag-and-drop.

### Choosing a data processing engine

| Situation | Choose | Why |
|-----------|--------|-----|
| Structured data and the transformation is expressible in SQL | **[BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/introduction)** | Serverless ANSI SQL; ELT inside the warehouse needs no separate engine |
| New pipeline, streaming or unified batch and streaming, no cluster operations | **Dataflow** | Beam code, autoscaling, managed |
| Existing Hadoop or Spark jobs, or need for the open-source ecosystem | **[Dataproc](https://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/concepts/overview)** (now Managed Service for Apache Spark) | Move jobs without rewriting; a serverless option exists |

Ask in order: can SQL do it (BigQuery), is it working Spark or Hadoop code (Dataproc), is it new or streaming (Dataflow). Run Dataproc clusters ephemerally; an idle cluster still bills. Anti-patterns: rewriting working Spark jobs into Beam under a deadline, and building a Beam pipeline for a transformation SQL handles.

### Data platform design: ingest, transform, share

Think in three steps: how data gets in, how it is transformed, how others consume it.

| Need | Choose | Catch |
|------|--------|-------|
| Continuous replication of row changes from MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB or Spanner into BigQuery, no pipeline code | **[Datastream](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/overview)** | Serverless CDC; replicates, never transforms |
| Custom in-flight logic, or a sink Datastream lacks | **Dataflow** | [Dataflow templates](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/faq) load Datastream's Cloud Storage output into BigQuery, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL or Spanner; you operate the pipeline |
| Move the database itself | **Database Migration Service** | [Destinations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/database-migration/docs/overview) are Cloud SQL and AlloyDB, not BigQuery |
| Occasional ad-hoc read of live operational data | **[Federated query](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/federated-queries-intro)** | Read-only, slower than BigQuery storage; repeated analytics belong on a replica |

**Datastream defaults and limits.** [Merge write mode](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/configure-bigquery-destination) is the default: the table mirrors the source, needs primary keys and keeps no history. Append-only keeps every change event for an audit trail. The staleness limit applies only to merge mode: [0 minutes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/create-a-stream) always queries the freshest data at the highest query cost, so relax it where minutes of lag are fine. Delivery is [at-least-once with no ordering guarantee](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/faq); deduplicate with the metadata. Maximum event size into BigQuery is [20 MB](https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastream/docs/destination-bigquery).

**[Dataform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/overview)** is the T in ELT: it transforms data already in BigQuery and does not extract or load. SQLX files (config block plus SQL body) compile to Standard SQL, in Git repositories connected to GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps Services or Bitbucket. `ref()` [builds the dependency graph](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/create-tables) and catches missing or circular dependencies. Table types are table, incremental, view and materialized; an incremental table with a `uniqueKey` merges rather than appends duplicates. [Assertions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dataform/docs/assertions) test quality: `nonNull`, `uniqueKey`, `rowConditions`, or a manual query that must return zero rows. Schedule with workflow configurations, Cloud Composer or Cloud Scheduler. Dataform [is free](https://cloud.google.com/dataform/pricing); you pay for the BigQuery queries it runs. Choose it for SQL transformations needing review, history and tests; Dataflow for streaming or Beam logic; Dataproc for existing Spark. Anti-pattern: cron-chained saved queries with no tests.

**Analytics Hub** (documented as [BigQuery sharing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/analytics-hub-introduction)) shares data across teams or organizations without replicating it. A publisher adds a **listing** referencing a **shared dataset** to an **exchange** (private or public); a subscriber gets a **linked dataset**, a read-only pointer queried live while the data stays in the publisher's project. Publishers pay storage, subscribers pay their queries. Egress restrictions block copy, clone, export, snapshot and `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT`; one shared dataset allows 1,000 linked datasets; authorized views are the best practice. Choose it over scheduled exports or copies (stale, duplicated storage, hard to revoke) and over direct access to the source dataset (no catalog, wider exposure).

For orchestration, [Workflows](https://cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/overview) is serverless, charges nothing while idle and combines Cloud Run, Cloud Run functions, Google Cloud APIs and any HTTP API; a workflow can retry, poll or wait for up to a year. [Managed Service for Apache Airflow](https://cloud.google.com/composer/docs/concepts/overview) (the evolution of Cloud Composer) is for Python Airflow DAGs that coordinate larger scheduled pipelines. Rule of thumb: Workflows for calling services and handling the results; Airflow when you need DAG-based scheduling of larger pipelines and the Airflow ecosystem. You may still see the name Cloud Composer on exam material.

On the API side, [API Gateway](https://cloud.google.com/api-gateway/docs/about-api-gateway) fronts backends (Cloud Run functions, Cloud Run, App Engine standard) with a REST interface defined by OpenAPI 2.0, handling authentication, traffic management and monitoring. [Apigee](https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/get-started/what-apigee) is the full API management platform: proxies, security policies, analytics, monetization and a developer portal for governed API programs.

Prefer asynchronous, loosely coupled integration. Synchronous calls chain the availability and latency of services together; composite availability is the product of the parts.

## Cost optimization

The [cost optimization pillar](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/framework/cost-optimization) has four principles: align spending with business value, foster cost awareness, optimize resource usage, and optimize continuously. The rule is *appropriate*, not *cheapest*.

| Lever | Best for | Watch out for |
|-------|----------|---------------|
| **Right-size** | Over-provisioned VMs | [Recommendations](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/apply-machine-type-recommendations-for-instances) use 8 days of metrics and are unavailable for memory-optimized, GPU and TPU instances |
| **Spot VMs** | Fault-tolerant, interruptible batch | [Up to 91% discount](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/spot), no SLA, may be unavailable; needs retries and checkpoints |
| **Committed use discounts** | Steady 24/7 baseline | One- or three-year terms, billed monthly whether used or not ([CUD overview](https://cloud.google.com/docs/cuds)) |
| **Scale down when idle** | Variable or periodic load | Cloud Run scales to zero; a MIG reaches zero only with schedule-based autoscaling and minimum replicas 0 |
| **Match resilience to criticality** | DR and HA spend | Tier workloads (Module 2) |

For a nightly, fault-tolerant pipeline with no tight deadline, use Spot VMs with idempotent, checkpointed tasks plus workers that scale down between runs. Three-year CUDs sized to peak, or always-on large VMs, waste money. Spanner multi-region is a resilience feature, not a cost one.

## KPIs and ROI

A good KPI is specific, measurable, time-bound and tied to an outcome. "Better performance" is not a KPI; "reduce p95 checkout latency from 1,200 ms to under 500 ms within 90 days of cutover" is: metric, baseline, target, deadline.

**ROI** = (benefit - cost) / cost. Benefits include lower TCO, faster time to market and fewer outages; costs include migration effort, dual-running, training and licenses. Example: a 400,000 migration that returns 400,000 a year in savings and avoided outages has 0% ROI after one year and 200% after three. Always state the time horizon. Define KPIs before the project, capture the baseline during assessment, and re-measure afterward.

## Cloud-first and future-proofing

- **Cloud-first means managed and serverless by default,** and buying commodity capabilities rather than building them. It is not cloud-only: retain what constraints require.
- **Make trade-offs consciously:** managed services trade some portability for speed; document the exit path.
- **Plan for growth.** Choose services that scale (Spanner, Bigtable, BigQuery) so 10x growth is configuration, not a rewrite.

### Flexibility, changing needs and new capabilities

**Flexible resources.** A [managed instance group](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/autoscaler) autoscales on CPU utilization, load balancing capacity, Cloud Monitoring metrics or schedules (up to 128 per group); predictive autoscaling scales out ahead of forecast load for slow-starting or cyclical workloads. Cloud Run scales to zero. A stopped VM can [change its machine type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/changing-machine-type-of-stopped-instance) with disk data preserved, but not inside a MIG or with Local SSD. Resource-based CUDs are tied to a region and to vCPU and memory amounts, while spend-based commitments are dollars per hour and span more usage. Commit only to the baseline you are sure of.

**Evolving business needs.** The framework's *design for change* principle opens with "No system is static": deliver small changes often, start with a minimal viable design, and revisit KPIs when strategy shifts. Stateless, decoupled components and infrastructure as code (Terraform) keep later replacement cheap.

**Adopting cloud improvements.** Managed services improve without you and names change (Vertex AI to Agent Platform). Keep configuration in code so a service swap is a change request, and review the architecture on a schedule.

## Current AI platform naming

| Name | What it is |
|------|-----------|
| **Gemini Cloud Assist** | AI assistance in the console, CLI and IDEs for design, troubleshooting and cost analysis |
| **Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform** | The current name for what was Vertex AI |
| **[Model Garden](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/start/introduction-unified-platform)** | Catalog to explore, test and deploy models from Google and partners |
| **[Model Armor](https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/model-armor-overview)** | Screens LLM prompts and responses for prompt injection, sensitive data, harmful content and malicious URLs; start inspect-only, then inspect-and-block |
| **[Agent Platform tooling](https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/overview)** | Agent Studio (low-code canvas), Agent Development Kit (code-first framework), Agent Runtime (managed deployment) |
| **[AI Hypercomputer](https://cloud.google.com/ai-hypercomputer/docs/overview)** | Integrated supercomputing system: GPUs and TPUs, networking, storage, open software, flexible consumption such as Spot VMs and reservations |

**Choosing a Gemini model.** The [model catalog](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/models) groups Gemini by family: Pro for complex reasoning, Flash for price-performance, Flash-Lite for the lowest latency and cost. Start with the smallest that meets your quality bar.

## Anti-patterns and common mistakes

- **Synchronous chains** between many services, so one slow dependency stalls everything.
- **Point-to-point integrations** where Pub/Sub fan-out would decouple producers and consumers.
- **Wrong orchestrator:** Airflow for a three-step API sequence, or Workflows replacing a DAG-heavy platform.
- **Dataflow where a visual tool is requested,** or Data Fusion where streaming control is required.
- **CUDs for variable or peak load,** and Spot for work that cannot be interrupted.
- **Qualitative KPIs** and ROI without a time horizon or baseline.
- **Copying or hand-building what a managed service does:** nightly dataset copies instead of Analytics Hub, custom CDC code instead of Datastream, cron-chained untested SQL instead of Dataform.
- **Treating cheapest as best,** sacrificing a required NFR.

## Exam tips

- **Pub/Sub for fan-out, Dataflow or Data Fusion for pipelines.** One event to many consumers is Pub/Sub; managed ETL is Dataflow (code) or Data Fusion (visual).
- **Batch plus fault-tolerant plus flexible deadline means Spot and scale-down,** not long-term commitments sized to peak or always-on large VMs.
- **CUDs are for steady baseline load;** you pay whether you use it or not.
- **A proper KPI has a metric, baseline, target and date.** ROI is (benefit - cost) / cost over a stated horizon.
- **Workflows for service orchestration, Airflow (formerly Cloud Composer) for DAG-based pipelines;** API Gateway for a simple REST front, Apigee for governed API management.
- **SQL-expressible transformation means BigQuery; existing Spark or Hadoop code means Dataproc; new or streaming pipelines mean Dataflow.**
- **Operational database changes into BigQuery with no pipeline code means Datastream** (merge for a mirror, append-only for history); Database Migration Service targets Cloud SQL or AlloyDB.
- **Versioned, tested SQL transformations inside BigQuery mean Dataform:** `ref()` builds dependencies, assertions test quality, and it does not ingest data.
- **Sharing BigQuery data across teams or organizations without copying means Analytics Hub:** exchange, listing, shared dataset, read-only linked dataset; publisher pays storage, subscriber pays queries.
- **Choose Gemini by family:** Pro for complex reasoning, Flash for price-performance, Flash-Lite for lowest latency and cost; Agent Studio is low-code, the Agent Development Kit is code-first.
- **Elasticity and change.** MIGs autoscale on CPU, load balancing capacity, metrics or schedules; Cloud Run scales to zero; commit only to the sure baseline.
- **Prefer managed, serverless, decoupled, stateless designs** and document the trade-offs; cloud-first does not mean cheapest or most portable.
- **Match the AI product to the job:** Gemini Cloud Assist for console help, Model Garden for models, Model Armor for prompt screening, AI Hypercomputer for AI infrastructure.
- **Cost optimization means appropriate spend.** Match resilience, capacity and discount commitments to the actual requirement.
